title: 25.3 AI-Enabled Design Space Discovery and End-to-End Synthesis for RFICs with Reinforcement Learning and Inverse Methods Demonstrating mm-Wave/sub-THz PAs Between 30 and 120GHz
problem: RF/mmWave IC design relies on intuitive, template-based architectures that limit exploration to small pre-fixed topologies. Circuit-EM co-design requires iterative trial-and-error optimization across transistor sizing, power-combining, matching-network design, and layout extraction. This severely restricts achievable performance and extends design time.
motivation: mm-Wave and sub-THz circuits demand exploration of non-intuitive design spaces beyond human templates to unlock novel topologies and superior PPA; reducing design time is critical for rapid technology prototyping.
method: An AI-enabled algorithmic flow combines reinforcement learning for architecture discovery and inverse EM synthesis for passive network design. The system automates circuit topology selection, parameter optimization, and layout generation from specifications to fabricated silicon without manual template selection or iterative simulation loops.
key_novelty: End-to-end AI-enabled RFIC synthesis with both active and passive optimization, from specifications to layout, demonstrating non-intuitive architectures.
contributions: First RFIC AI synthesis demonstrating fabricated results for active+passive co-optimization
100-120GHz sub-THz PA: 12.6dBm P_sat with high efficiency
Eliminates manual iterative design loops and template-based architecture selection
baselines: Simulation-based parameter optimization for low-frequency circuits
limitations: Not discussed; design automation time, convergence robustness, and generalization to different PA topologies/frequencies not fully characterized.
primary_theme: AI-enabled RFIC design space discovery and synthesis
